What’s in this example?

Illustrative 120-credit residential bachelor’s degree

The same course load is used on both sides. A short final term is priced using the school’s published part-time rules where applicable.

  • University charges shown: $25,390. Outside-credit budget used: $2,000.
  • The maximum is 75% of a degree. Approved transfer credit must also satisfy major/minor residency, prerequisites, and the receiving catalog. No blanket 30-credit ACE-course cap was established; the Experience Plus limit is a different policy.
  • Policy illustration. Build your exact course plan to see which credits could apply.

Tuition only: the example excludes the $460 activity fee and $170 health fee per semester, the $100 degree-completion fee, housing, dining, books, and other personal/program charges. Financial aid and discounts can change the comparison.

At 15 credits per semester, 120 university credits model eight semesters; 30 remaining credits model two semesters, or one academic year of university work. Outside study, evaluation, admissions, prerequisites, and course availability add time.

At least 25% of the degree and major/minor must be completed through Liberty. The 90-credit figure is a policy ceiling; each course must apply to the exact degree.

Outside-course spending is an editable allowance, not a quoted or school-approved package. Prices are held constant for comparison; future rates and financial aid can change the result.

A few questions you might have.

Can I start without any college credits?

Yes. Start with a degree plan from zero. You can add past courses or transcripts later.

What if I already have college credits?

Upload your transcript or a spreadsheet, review your courses together, and compare where they fit. Your course collection stays with you when you change degrees.

Is this only for online degrees?

No. Explore online and on-campus plans. Each route keeps the receiving college’s transfer and graduation requirements in view.

Will my college accept these courses?

Our researched plans use published course matches and school policies, with sources you can open. The college makes the official decision about your own transfer credits.

What does DegreeSteps cost?

Building and saving your degree plan is free. Courses, college tuition and provider fees are separate. Sign in to save your plan to your account.
